rows.text: For the boundary-index convention $J\ne\varnothing$ and the complex punctured-tube realization, take $U=\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$: all nonempty boundary strata are points, the maquette is three isolated vertices, and the punctured tube retracts onto three circles. rows.text: The “flèche en sens inverse” compares a groupoid made from points and arcs with one made from coverings, and the author expressly omits the details. A genuine construction should assign a fibre functor to each normal direction and transport along paths, then verify independence and composition; Deligne's curve result has the same comparison objective but explicitly treats the classical construction only for curves (Deligne, 1989, §15.3).

rows.text: “Je ne vois pas clairement à présent dans quelle mesure le th. envisagé est indispensable” opens a different route: use the punctured-germ groupoids themselves as the basic objects. This differs from the definition $\widetilde\Pi_{\Delta_r}=\Pi_1P^*_{\Delta_r}$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 131, while retaining the missing-generization objective of scans 133–135. The change may remove a comparison theorem from the construction, but it transfers the proof obligation to the claimed extension structure and to the compatibility of its lattice quotients; the note records this as the author's proposed reorganization, not as an established equivalence of frameworks.

rows.heading: 138-24 — Scan 148, l. 7 — unpursued implication
rows.text: The phrase “de noyau un quotient de $T_{d_0,\ldots,d_r}$” is consistent with the exact sequence $\pi_2(B)\to\pi_1((\mathbb C^*)^r)\to\pi_1(P)\to\pi_1(B)\to1$ for a locally trivial torus bundle over a connected base. It qualifies the extension description in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 130–131, where the margin already warns that the full lattice kernel requires a condition on $\pi_2$. The connecting homomorphism can kill meridians, so a proof should identify its image and the induced local-system action rather than assert an injection of the entire lattice; the fibration exact sequence is the relevant classical result (Serre, 1949–1950, §1).

rows.heading: 138-28 — Scan 150, l. 14 — unproved claim
rows.text: The “Th de recollement” claims an equivalence of topoi between the colimit of the flag-indexed punctured germs and $X^{*\infty}$. It adds a descent theorem to the half-simplicial groupoid programme in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131–135, and is stronger than the fundamental-group calculations associated with gluing in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–169. A proof must specify the categorical colimit, establish effective descent for sheaves along the augmented flag system, and explain how the local normal-crossing models cover the boundary germ; a comparison of $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ alone proves less than the stated theorem.

rows.heading: 138-30 — Scans 139–150, especially 148, l. 7 — unpursued implication
rows.text: The repeated demand for generization and a “structure d'extension” has a concrete application to the earlier programme of recovering the moduli groupoids and their graph operations. These pages add geometric machinery to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 104, which asks to determine $\Pi_1M_{g,I}$, the extensions $S\Pi_1M_G$, and the maps induced by graph generization, and to scans 78–89, where those extensions are already organized around boundary germs. A useful comparison would track a single node-smoothing meridian through the normal torsor, the punctured germ, and the graph-generization map, checking its orientation, kernel, and permutation action before asserting that the abstract gluing construction realizes the full earlier programme.

rows.heading: 151-04 — Scan 152 — MPL_147_138-190_scan152.tex, lines 3–12, (246) — unproved claim

It **adds** this collapse to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131 and 133, which distinguish the partially functorial ordinary stratum groupoids from the proposed semisimplicial system of punctured-normal groupoids. A complete proof must specify the colimit convention and the comparison functor, then show that removing the higher strata and replacing the surviving diagram preserve the relevant fundamental groupoid; the objectwise descriptions of the $\widetilde\Pi$'s do not by themselves establish that conclusion. The formula targets the boundary $V^*_{\Theta,X}$, and scan 156 explicitly explains why such a formula can contain no ambient-space reconstruction in the curve case.

This **adds** a closed-subset classification to the branch-labeling torsors of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 109 and 117, where permutation monodromy is already built into the flag spaces. To prove both directions one must show that the component selections respect the incidence maps and descend to a locally finite union of branch intersections, and that every such union yields exactly those selections. Working with $\pi_0(D_d)$ incorporates the global branch identifications; independently labeling local branches without their transport could produce a selection that does not descend.

rows.heading: 151-17 — Scan 156 — MPL_147_138-190_scan156.tex, lines 5–18, (254) — unproved claim
rows.text: The assertion expressing “$\Pi_1(X)$ … comme somme amalgamée” is the curve case of gluing the complement to genuine neighborhoods of the missing points. It **restates** the cospan and hole-filling construction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 162 and 168, with the closed-point groupoids now discrete. For an actual open tubular-neighborhood cover, Brown’s Theorem 3.4 proves the fundamental-groupoid pushout using an object set meeting every component of the overlap, so disconnected punctured neighborhoods cause no problem (Brown, 1967, pp. 391–392). Passage from those actual neighborhoods to the manuscript’s germ topoi still requires the relevant fundamental-groupoid comparison; the theorem does not assert an equivalence of topoi.

rows.heading: 151-18 — Scan 156 — MPL_147_138-190_scan156.tex, lines 5–10 and 13–18, (254) — unpursued implication
rows.text: The right-hand “groupoïde discret” makes the new leg kill the loop around each missing point, so after choosing paths to a basepoint the proposed formula becomes the quotient of $\pi_1(X\setminus\Theta)$ by the normal closure of the meridians. This **restates**, in the complex-curve case, the explicit quotient by the normal subgroup generated by the images of $\ker\sigma_i$ in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 169. Brown’s groupoid relations also provide this calculation under the open-cover hypotheses (Brown, 1967, Corollary 3.6, p. 393). Keeping the transport paths or the groupoid formulation is necessary to interpret the meridians consistently when the divisor has several points.

rows.heading: 151-19 — Scans 156–157 — MPL_147_138-190_scan156.tex, (254); MPL_147_138-190_scan157.tex, lines 2 and 18 — unpursued implication
rows.text: The deleted remark that the right arrow “n’a pas encore reçu droit de cité” records a deficiency that survives in the live request to introduce the missing structural elements. It **adds** a demand for the meridian-killing leg to the earlier generization formalism, while `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, already distinguishes an actual open-neighborhood inclusion from a map factored through the closed stratum and retains a noninvertible comparison transformation. These are different types of data: the right leg of (254) is a functor of fundamental groupoids, whereas the transformation $\alpha$ belongs to the richer topos recollement. Recovering the former therefore does not justify replacing the latter by an isomorphism when constructing all the desired topoi.

rows.heading: 151-27 — Scan 160 — MPL_147_138-190_scan160.tex, lines 11–17 — unpursued implication
rows.text: The admission that the reduction “ne s’explicite pas aisément, au niveau des groupoïdes fondamentaux” concerns information lost when passing from a closed immersion of topoi to its induced groupoid map. It **restates** the distinction between the mixed recollement topos and its multigaloisian reflection in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, and **adds** the concrete problem of recovering open complements from that reduced data. A simple illustration is that both pairs $(\mathbb C,\{0\})$ and $(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ induce, up to equivalence, the same arrow of trivial connected fundamental groupoids, while their open complements have respectively fundamental group $\mathbb Z$ and no objects. This illustration concerns the bare groupoid arrow, and scan 180 supplies a separate warning about higher cohomology lost by a proposed constructible reconstruction; neither warning identifies the comparison in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 167, with the one refuted on 180.

rows.heading: 151-33 — Scans 161–163 — MPL_147_138-190_scan161.tex, (260); MPL_147_138-190_scan162.tex, line 3; MPL_147_138-190_scan163.tex, lines 4–54 — own idea
rows.text: The relative “pièces de construction” suggest testing a description by exit-path data that retains directed specialization and its homotopies, rather than using only the separate fundamental groupoids of the pieces. This proposal **adds** a possible organization of the flag tubes to the noninvertible recollement transformation of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, while respecting that file’s distinction, on scan 166, between the mixed topos and its galoisian reflection. Treumann’s exit-path classifications supply comparison targets under conical-stratification and tameness hypotheses; identifying these germ flags with exit paths remains a separate task (Treumann, 2009, Theorems 1.2 and 7.14). Confidence is medium because the needed specialization data are present in the program; constructing the comparison and checking the stratification hypotheses remain necessary, and scan 180 rules out concluding that a constructible category of sets alone recovers the ambient homotopy type.

rows.heading: 164-17 — Scan 172; `MPL_147_138-190_scan172.tex`, lines 4–6 — conjecture — The variance program remains unfinished
rows.text: “Je voudrais maintenant expliciter la variance” leaves the allowed morphisms and their effect on $\Pi_1$ as an explicit program before the discussion turns to normal bundles. It **restates and enlarges** the missing generization construction in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 132–135, where only maps preserving the first vertex are formal and the other face map requires new geometry. A proof should specify the indexing category, construct the elementary face morphisms, and show their compatibility with composition, degeneracies if retained, and the newly introduced partial puncturings. Objectwise homotopy models from (294) will not supply this variance unless the comparison maps themselves have the required coherent naturality.

rows.heading: 164-31 — Scans 175–176, qualified by scan 178; `MPL_147_138-190_scan175.tex`, lines 14–30, and `MPL_147_138-190_scan176.tex`, (294) — unpursued implication — The inertia lattice can acquire a quotient
rows.text: The torus-fiber model does not imply an injection of the entire lattice $\mathbb Z^r$ into the fundamental group of the total space. This **restates** the caveat in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 88 and especially scan 130, whose margins require vanishing $\pi_2$ before claiming an extension by the full twisted lattice. For a locally trivial bundle with fiber $(\mathbb C^*)^r$, the homotopy exact sequence gives $\pi_2(B)\to\mathbb Z^r\to\pi_1(E)\to\pi_1(B)\to1$, with the appropriate monodromy on the fiber lattice (Serre, 1949–1950, §1). rows.heading: 179-03 — The antecedent of “cette reconstitution”
rows.text: The margin expects “cette reconstitution” independently of further hypotheses of the $K(\pi,1)$ kind, but does not securely identify which of the preceding reconstructions it means. It **differs in scope** from `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–168, where formal recollement of a mixed topos, groupoid amalgamation, and comparison with the original geometric topos are separate operations. Read with the immediate “Remords,” the margin may preserve the formal reconstruction of the mixed topos while withdrawing its identification with the original homotopy type; the uncertain abbreviation and antecedent should remain open rather than turning the margin into a universal theorem.

rows.heading: 180-01 — The sphere obstruction and the remaining recollement question
rows.text: ### 180-01 — The sphere obstruction and the remaining recollement question

rows.heading: 180-01 — The sphere obstruction and the remaining recollement question
rows.text: The “contre-exemple type” shows that the indicated constructible-sheaf topos on $S^2=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ has the single-arrow description while the sphere retains positive-dimensional cohomology, and ends by asking how to understand the homotopy type of a topos obtained by “recollement”. This **adds** an explicit geometric obstruction to the open comparison questions of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 167–168, rather than supplying an obstruction to recollement as a formal construction. The cohomological contrast should be tested with an identified coefficient object — for instance the constant integral coefficient — and an identified comparison morphism, since arbitrary coefficient cohomology and the shape of a topos are not interchangeable assertions.

rows.heading: 180-05 — Which of the earlier acyclicity hopes fails?
rows.text: The contrast with “celle de $S^2$” should be located in the correct stage of the earlier comparison. `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 167, tentatively expects acyclicity for $B_{X;S}\to B_{\Pi_1X}$, whereas scan 168 separately discusses the original geometric topos mapping to $B_{X;S}$, so the present example **adds** an obstruction to the latter comparison without contradicting the former expectation in this case. Indeed the single-arrow category and the terminal groupoid both have contractible classifying spaces, while the original sphere does not; this distinction prevents a false retrospective contradiction between the two manuscripts.

rows.heading: 182-03 — Separatedness is distinct from effective gluing
rows.text: The deletion of “séparé” in favour of “un faisceau,” together with the margin read uncertainly as “est connue quand on la connaît localement,” suggests that uniqueness from local data is being distinguished from existence of a global representative. This **adds** a descent question to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106–108, where an ambient global divisor already supplies the representative, and **differs** from the categorical recollement of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 163–166, which does not settle separatedness of this presheaf of partitions. The relevant question is whether connectedness forces two global partitions with the same local component data to coincide even when compatible local partitions fail to form one admissible global partition. The decisive marginal wording remains uncertain, so this is a proposed interpretation of the revision, not a corrected reading.

rows.heading: 105-R3 — Reading question — Deck transformations and the opposite-group convention
rows.text: At scan 105, manuscript page 52, (2) defines the precise group by $\pi_1(X;\widetilde X)=\operatorname{Aut}_X(\widetilde X)$. This **restates** the representing-cover viewpoint in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 8–10**, where the covariant fibre functor is $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(S,T)$, but those passages do not explicitly settle the left/right convention in the present formula. Precomposition on $F(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(\widetilde X,W)$ reverses composition, so it identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_X(\widetilde X)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$; using the inverse deck transformation instead gives a left action, exactly the convention issue made explicit in the proof of Lemma 58.3.9 (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BMQ). Confidence: high in the composition calculation and medium in the manuscript's intended convention; the equality need not be called erroneous, but this choice should be fixed before comparing later conjugation and cyclotomic-action formulas.

rows.heading: 106-R1 — Reading question — Algebraic closure inside a separably closed field
rows.text: At scan 106, display (4) and its following sentence, “la clôture alg. de $k(x)$ dans $\Omega$” accompanies a canonical comparison whose first subscript remains $\alpha$ or $X$. This **adds** a larger separably closed field of a base point to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 22**, which describes a separable residue-field closure, and scan 108 of the present manuscript itself explicitly says “clôtures séparables dans $\Omega$”. Finite étale residue extensions factor through the separable algebraic closure inside $\Omega$, giving the fibre-functor comparison for the fixed scheme $X$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.6.3, Tag 0BQ8), but a merely separably closed $\Omega$ need not contain an algebraic closure in the purely inseparable sense. Confidence: high in this distinction, medium in the intended terminology, and low in the marked subscript; it does not assert invariance of $\pi_1(X_\Omega)$ under changing the base field of $X$.

rows.heading: 107-C1 — Unproved claim — A simply connected scheme as a base point
rows.text: At scan 107, manuscript page 53, the parenthesis before (7), “plus gén. $\mathcal E_Y^Z$ chaque fois qu'on a un $Y$-schéma $Z$ $1$-connexe”, proposes a fibre functor based on $Z$. This **adds** a scheme over $Y$ to the representing-object formulation in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 8, Proposition 1.5**, and to its pointed-cover formulation in scans 9–10. For finite étale covers, the construction is precise when $Z$ is nonempty and connected with trivial étale fundamental group: send a cover $W\to Y$ to $\pi_0(W\times_Y Z)$, since every such pullback is a finite disjoint union of copies of $Z$, and use Galois-category reconstruction for its automorphism group (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BMQ and 0BQ8). Confidence: high for this finite-étale formulation; extending the same wording to all locally constant objects requires retaining the context's separate hypotheses on the topos.

rows.heading: 107-R1 — Reading question — The index of the classifying group
rows.text: At scan 107, manuscript page 53, the phrase “pour le topos $B_{\pi(X)}$ des rev étales de $Y$” leaves a possible mismatch between $X$ and $Y$. Its intended fibre-functor role **restates** **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 11–12**, where a morphism of multigaloisian topoi is related to the corresponding fundamental groupoids. For covers of connected $Y$, standard reconstruction uses $\pi_1(Y)$ and its finite continuous sets (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Theorem 58.6.2, Tag 0BQ8), but that mathematical expectation is only an interpretive alternative, not evidence for replacing the frozen $\pi(X)$ reading. Confidence: high that the index matters, low that context alone resolves it.

rows.heading: 109-Q1 — Reading question — What does “universal” exactness include?
rows.text: At scan 109, manuscript page 54, “une ‘suite exacte d'homotopie universelle’ … (en dim $1$)” introduces the hypothesis used in (12)–(13). This **adds** a universal relative assertion to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 188**, whose specific curve-moduli fibration explicitly retains a preceding $\pi_2$-term before obtaining a short exact sequence. The standard scheme theorem for a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation with connected reduced geometric fibres gives $\pi_1(X_{\bar y})\to\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y)\to 1$, with no initial $1$, so ordinary exactness, injectivity from the fibre, and invariance under the proposed changes of $T$ must be distinguished (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Proposition 58.15.2, Tag 0C0J). Confidence: high that the manuscript needs a stronger or more explicit hypothesis for its fibre-group isomorphisms; no claim is made that the author intended only the weaker standard theorem.

rows.heading: 110-C1 — Unproved claim — The arithmetic sequence and the stronger assertion about $T$
rows.text: At scan 110, after (13), “Cette hypothèse sera tjrs satisfaite si $Y=\operatorname{Spec}K$ … si $X$ est géom. $0$-connexe” **restates** the arithmetic/geometric extension framework of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 22 and 47**, while (12) **adds** identification with the group of $X_T$. The arithmetic statement is valid for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated $X/K$ with connected geometric fibre: $1\to\pi_1(X_{\bar K})\to\pi_1(X)\to G_K\to 1$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.14.3, Tag 0BTX). It does not justify the stronger assertion for every simply connected $T$, and unrestricted field extension of a nonproper scheme in characteristic $p$ already supplies a counterexample, detailed in 110-O1 (Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). Confidence: high in the arithmetic theorem and in the distinction between it and the unrestricted reading of (12).

rows.heading: 110-O1 — Own idea — A test of the universal wording in positive characteristic
rows.text: For the “tjrs satisfaite” assertion on scan 110 after (13), take $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, $X=\mathbf A^1_k$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $\Omega=\overline{k(t)}$, and the section $x=0$. The Artin–Schreier cover $z^p-z=tx$ of $X_T$ gives a class in $\Omega[x]/\{h^p-h\}$ outside the image of $k[x]/\{h^p-h\}$, so the natural $\pi_1(X_T)\to\pi_1(X)$ cannot be an isomorphism although $T$ is $1$-connected (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0A3J; compare the same obstruction in Landesman, 2024, Example 1.7). This **differs** from the characteristic-zero curve setting of **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 19–22**, and does not affect scan 106's change of the field of a base point while keeping $X$ fixed. Confidence: high, because polynomial Artin–Schreier classes detect the failure explicitly; this is an application of a known obstruction to the manuscript's wording, not a claim of a new counterexample in the literature.

rows.heading: 111-C1 — Unproved claim — The connected-component factor and its size
rows.text: At scan 111, manuscript page 55, (14)–(16) assert a “factorisation can.” with $Y'$ “étale fini ou pro-étale fini” and explicitly replace $X\times_YT$ by $X\times_{Y'}T$. This **adds** a relative component factor to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 83**, where a finite base extension separates geometric connected components and makes the relevant images over the base Galois group explicit. A precise finite case is the Stein factorization of a proper flat finitely presented map with geometrically reduced fibres, for which $Y'\to Y$ is finite étale (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Lemma 58.15.1, Tag 0BUN); the closed image of $\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y)$ instead determines a pointed profinite cover in Galois theory, without automatically being an open subgroup or a finite cover. Confidence: high in these two constructions, with the fibre identification still subject to the exactness qualifications in 109-Q1.

rows.heading: 112-C1 — Unproved claim — The kernel over the universal cover
rows.text: At scan 112, (17) is explicitly “sans hyp. de suite exacte” and the inserted expression in (18) identifies the relative group with the group of $X_{\widetilde Y}$. This **adds** a relative-kernel construction to **LM_140-2_text.tex, scans 9–11**, which identify pointed universal covers with fibre functors and their functorial transport. In the finite-étale pro-cover interpretation, pullback to the universal cover of $Y$, followed by the connected component selected by the chosen lift, corresponds to the closed subgroup $\ker(\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y))$; this is a formal subgroup construction, distinct from asserting that an arbitrary geometric fibre has that group (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tags 0BMQ and 0BTV). Confidence: high with that selected component and pro-object interpretation, which the diagram through $Y'$ records.

rows.heading: 120-O1 — Own idea — Infinity on the affine line
rows.text: For “A t-on une réciproque ?” on scan 120, take $K=\mathbf C$, $L=\mathbf C(t)$, $U=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf C}$, and the valuation at infinity on $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf C}$. Its nontrivial inertia maps trivially to $\pi_1(U)=1$, since the complex affine line is simply connected and the étale group is its profinite completion, but the unique center of the valuation on the proper model is $\infty\notin U$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Section 64.27, “Comparison,” Tag 03VD, and Lemma 58.13.5, Tag 0BUA). This **differs** from the restricted curve classes in **LM_140-2_text.tex, scan 20**, and is permitted by scan 115's explicit allowance for algebraically closed $K$. Confidence: high because both the trivial target group and the missing center are explicit; the example does not disprove the additional marginal restriction, and the same test can be transferred to $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Q}$ using characteristic-zero base-change invariance and the arithmetic sequence (Landesman, 2024, Theorem 1.1; The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0BTX).

rows.heading: 128-Q1 — conjecture
rows.text: The author asks how far the image of valuation inertia in the geometric group of one model distinguishes valuations, comparing it with a group at an end. This adds passage through the quotient to a chosen model to the curve-puncture separation discussion of `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 117–118; separation of cusp inertia in a hyperbolic curve is a more restricted fact (Stix, 2012, Proposition 16). The distinction between a subgroup of the full $G_L$ and its image in $\pi_1(U_{\bar K})$ is essential, as the equal-image example in 128-O2 shows.

rows.heading: 138-08 — Scan 142, ll. 3–8, (235) — conjecture
rows.text: The extension to “une immersion locale de topos” is qualified by “sauf erreur,” so the general topos construction is not established here. It adds a new neighborhood operation to the site-independent flag axioms of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 118–119, and to the tentative topos interpretation of germ coverings in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 242–243. One must define the intended class of immersions and the relevant limit of localizations, then prove that composition supplies the indicated morphism of germs; the existence of slice topoi alone does not settle that neighborhood problem (Artin et al., 1972, Exposé IV, §5).

rows.heading: 151-32 — Scan 163 — MPL_147_138-190_scan163.tex, lines 30–54, (263); continuation on scan 164 — unpursued implication
rows.text: The “quatre pièces” are the global open stratum $\mathbb C^*$, the point $P$, the disk germ $\mathbb D$, and its punctured germ $\mathbb D^*$, with the list completed on scan 164. This **restates** the difference between a germ and its residual germ in `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scan 245, and **adds** their placement beside global pieces in the flag construction. In particular, $V_0=V_0^*=\mathbb C^*$ does not already include the recovered ambient $\mathbb C$, and a disk germ has not been identified with its center as a topos merely because their ordinary fundamental groupoids are equivalent. The word “germe,” inserted in place of “disque,” keeps the neighborhood-filter information that the construction requires.

rows.heading: 164-02 — Scan 164; `MPL_147_138-190_scan164.tex`, lines 4–22, (264)–(265) — unpursued implication — A point and a disc serve different gluing roles
rows.text: The list distinguishes “point” from “germe de disque,” although their ordinary homotopy types agree after choosing a disc representative. This **restates**, in a particularly small model, the distinction in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 164–165, between the closed-stratum topos $B_S$, the mixed neighborhood topos $B_{D;S}$, and their different canonical maps. A replacement of the disc by the point is therefore justified only after specifying which invariant is being retained and what happens to the punctured-disc attachment. The four-object diagram should be tested at the level of its maps and gluing functors, since an equivalence of individual homotopy types alone does not supply the asserted reconstruction.

rows.heading: 164-21 — Scans 173–174; `MPL_147_138-190_scan173.tex`, lines 3–5 and 39–48, and `MPL_147_138-190_scan174.tex`, lines 25–34 — unproved claim — Descent from local immersions to flag-space bundles
